'''Ermanno Angelo Bencivenga''' is an Italian philosopher and Professor Emeritus of Philosophy at the [[University of California, Irvine]]. Bencivenga is known for his works on [[logic]], ethics, and [[political philosophy]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Forman |first1=David |title=Review of Ethics Vindicated: Kant's Transcendental Legitimation of Moral Discourse |journal=NDPR |date=19 June 2007 |url=https://ndpr.nd.edu/reviews/ethics-vindicated-kant-s-transcendental-legitimation-of-moral-discourse/ |language=en |issn=1538-1617}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dore |first1=Clement |title=Book Review: Ermanno Bencivenga Logic and Other Nonsense: The Case of Anselm and His God |journal=Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic |date=1 July 1994 |volume=35 |issue=3 |doi=10.1305/ndjfl/1040511352|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brittan |first1=Gordon G. |title=Review of Kant's Copernican Revolution |journal=Philosophy and Phenomenological Research |date=1992 |volume=52 |issue=3 |pages=740–742 |doi=10.2307/2108223 |jstor=2108223 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2108223 |issn=0031-8205|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Biography==
After graduating in philosophy from the [[University of Milan|State University of Milan]], Bencivenga soon left Italy, moving first to Canada for PhD studies and then to the United States, 
where he embarked on his academic career teaching, since 1979, at the [[University of California, Irvine]]. 

Several of his contributions have appeared over the years in various Italian newspapers like the ''[[La Stampa]]'', ''[[il Sole 24 Ore]]'', and ''[[l'Unità]]''.<ref>{{Cite web | title = Ermanno Bencivenga | website = SWIFT – Sito web italiano per la filosofia | url = http://www.swif.uniba.it/lei/rassegna//benciven.htm | access-date = 2023-12-07 | archive-date = 2012-06-13 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120613022512/http://www.swif.uniba.it/lei/rassegna//benciven.htm | url-status = dead }}</ref>

Since 2021 he hosts on the Italian television channel [[Byoblu]] the programs titled ''Spazio d'Illusione'' (Space of Illusion), dedicated to the [[history of cinema]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.google.com/search?q=bencivenga+%22spazio+di+illusione%22|title=Spazio di illusione|language=it|author=Ermanno Bencivenga|publisher=Byoblu}}</ref> and ''Spazio di Libertà'' (Space of Freedom), which is dedicated to philosophical issues.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GsPqnbYw1hE|title=Spazio di libertà|author=Ermanno Bencivenga|date=20 September 2021 |language=it|publisher=Byoblu}}</ref>

He currently speaks Italian, English, French, Spanish, and German. He also knows [[Latin]] and [[Ancient Greek]].

==Books==
* ''Kant's Copernican Revolution''. New York: Oxford University Press, 1987. 
* ''Looser Ends: The Practice of Philosophy''. Minneapolis: University of Minnesota Press, 1989. 
* ''The Discipline of Subjectivity: An Essay on Montaigne''. Princeton: Princeton University Press, 1990. 
* ''Logic and Other Nonsense: The Case of Anselm and His God''. Princeton: Princeton University Press, 1993. 
* ''Philosophy in Play''. Indianapolis: Hackett, 1994. 
* ''My Kantian Ways''. Berkeley: University of California Press, 1995. 
* ''A Theory of Language and Mind''. Berkeley: University of California Press 1997. 
* ''Freedom: A Dialogue''. Indianapolis: Hackett, 1997. 
* ''Hegel's Dialectical Logic''. New York: Oxford University Press, 2000. 
* ''Exercises in Constructive Imagination''. Dordrecht: Kluwer, 2001. 
* ''Dancing Souls''. Lanham (MD): Lexington Books, 2003. 
* ''Ethics Vindicated: Kant's Transcendental Legitimation of Moral Discourse''. New York: Oxford University Press, 2007. 
* ''Theories of the Logos''. Springer, 2017.
* ''Understanding Edgar Allan Poe: They Who Dream by Day''. Newcastle upon Tyne UK: Cambridge Scholars, 2023.
